common_mistake.incorrect_code:
interface Result
class Success(val value: Int) : Result
class Failure(val error: String) : Result
common_mistake.explanation: An interface allows any class to implement Result from anywhere, so a when over Result cannot be exhaustive and adding a case at runtime is possible. Sealed classes keep the hierarchy closed and exhaustive.

teaching_questions: When would you choose a sealed class over an interface?
What happens to existing when-expressions when you add a new subclass?
